examples.ko: 옆집 소리가 시끄러워서 귀마개를 끼고 잤어요.
examples.en: The neighbors were noisy, so I slept with earplugs in.
Did you pack the earplugs for swimming too?
In winter you really need warm earmuffs.

examples.ko: 귀마개 없이는 도서관에서도 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: Without earplugs I can't concentrate even in the library.
Sorry, could you lend me a pair of earplugs?

examples.ko: 이 귀마개는 부드러워서 오래 껴도 안 아파요.
examples.en: These earplugs are soft, so they don't hurt even if I wear them for a long time.

explain: 소음을 막는 것, 수영할 때 쓰는 것, 추위를 막는 것을 모두 '귀마개'라고 불러요. 그래서 어떤 귀마개인지는 문장 속 상황으로 알 수 있어요. 보통 '귀마개를 끼다, 귀마개를 하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: Earplugs for noise, for swimming, and earmuffs for the cold are all called '귀마개'. You tell which one is meant from the situation in the sentence. People usually say '귀마개를 끼다' or '귀마개를 하다'.

examples.en: The wind blew and my hair got all messed up.

examples.ko: 빗에 붙은 머리털을 하나씩 떼어 냈어요.
examples.en: I took the hairs stuck on the comb off one by one.
A baby's hair is very soft.
There is a lot of dust on your hair.
Even my hair got soaked, so I dried it with a towel.
My older brother has a lot of hair and is tall too.

explain: '머리카락'과 같은 뜻으로 쓰지만, 한 올씩 셀 때는 '머리카락 한 올'이라고 해요. 말할 때는 그냥 '머리'라고도 해서 '머리가 길어요'처럼 말해요. 머리 위의 털 전체를 말하는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It can be used like '머리카락', but when counting single strands you say '머리카락 한 올'. In speech people often just say '머리', as in '머리가 길어요'. 머리털 has the feel of all the hair on the head.

examples.en: I'm worried because my belly fat has increased lately.
I walk every day to lose belly fat.
Belly fat doesn't go away all at once.
My pants got tight because of my belly fat.
I cut back on snacks because I'm watching my belly fat.
I wonder if exercise reduces belly fat too.

explain: '배'와 '살'이 만나 사이시옷이 붙어 '뱃살'이 돼요. 배에 붙은 살이나 지방을 이야기할 때 써요. 다른 사람의 몸에 쓰면 평가처럼 들릴 수 있어서 조심하는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: '배' and '살' join with a linking ㅅ to become '뱃살'. Use it for fat on the stomach. Saying it about another person's body can sound like a judgment, so be careful.

examples.en: My knuckles are thick, so rings don't fit over them.

examples.ko: 손마디는 어릴 때 다쳐서 약간 휘었어요.
examples.en: My finger joint got hurt as a child and is slightly bent.

examples.ko: 일을 오래 했더니 손마디마다 굳은살이 박였어요.
examples.en: After working for a long time, I got calluses on every finger joint.
When you crack your knuckles, they make a sound.
Deep wrinkles are carved into Grandma's finger joints.
I put a bandage between the finger joints.

explain: 손가락이 꺾이는 마디 부분을 말해요. '손가락 마디'라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요. '마디'는 나무나 대나무의 마디에도 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It means the joint parts where the fingers bend. People also spell it out as '손가락 마디'. '마디' is also the word used for the joints of trees and bamboo.

examples.en: If breathing is hard, please open the window.
I practice breathing before I exercise.
Breathing is very important for health.
I have a cold, so even breathing is uncomfortable.
If you breathe slowly, your mind relaxes.
Breathing and walking are the easiest exercises.

explain: '숨쉬기 운동'처럼 연습이나 운동 이름 앞에 잘 붙어요. 아파서 숨 쉬기 힘들 때는 '숨이 차다', '숨이 막히다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It attaches easily before names of practice or exercise, as in '숨쉬기 운동'. When it is hard to breathe because of illness, say '숨이 차다' or '숨이 막히다'.

examples.en: The sleeves were long, so I folded them up.
Coffee got on my white sleeve.
The child wiped tears with a sleeve.
Winter sleeves have fur on the inside.
I rolled up my sleeves and started the dishes.
The ends of this shirt's sleeves are worn.

explain: 일상에서는 줄여서 그냥 '소매'라고 많이 해요. '소매를 걷다', '소매 끝'처럼 자주 써요. 팔 부분만 따로 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: In daily talk people often shorten it to just '소매'. It appears in phrases like '소매를 걷다' (roll up one's sleeves) and '소매 끝' (sleeve end). It names just the arm part of a garment.

examples.en: My upper lip is swollen and hurts.
When it's cold, I put lip balm on my upper lip.
I have a habit of biting my upper lip when I worry.
You have a milk mark above your upper lip.
The upper lip is thin and the lower lip is full.
Try pressing your upper and lower lips together and then parting them.

explain: 반대말은 '아랫입술'이에요. '윗'을 쓰고 [윈닙쑬]로 발음해요. 'ㅁ, ㅂ, ㅍ' 소리를 낼 때 입술을 붙이는 설명에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The opposite is '아랫입술' (lower lip). It is written with '윗' and pronounced [윈닙쑬]. It often appears in explanations of how to make the sounds ㅁ, ㅂ and ㅍ.

examples.en: Today I came wearing a black pleated skirt.
A pleated skirt sways prettily when the wind blows.

examples.ko: 교복 주름치마가 너무 짧아서 길이를 늘렸어요.
examples.en: My uniform pleated skirt was too short, so I lengthened it.
I'm looking for a blouse that goes with a pleated skirt.

examples.ko: 주름치마 주름이 풀리지 않게 조심해서 빨아 주세요.
examples.en: Please wash the pleated skirt carefully so the pleats don't come undone.

examples.ko: 언니가 물려준 주름치마가 아직도 잘 맞아요.
examples.en: The pleated skirt my sister handed down still fits well.

explain: '플리츠 스커트'와 같은 옷이에요. 옷 가게에서는 외래어도 들을 수 있지만, 일상 대화에서는 '주름치마'라고 해도 다 통해요.
explain_en: It is the same garment as a '플리츠 스커트' (pleated skirt). You may hear the loanword in clothing shops, but '주름치마' is understood in everyday talk.

examples.en: The taste stayed on the tip of my tongue for a long time.
I lightly licked the ice cream with the tip of my tongue.
That name is just on the tip of my tongue.
The words came right up to my tongue, but I held back.

examples.ko: 혀끝을 윗니 뒤에 대고 발음해 보세요.
examples.en: Try pronouncing it with the tip of your tongue behind the upper teeth.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 차를 마셨더니 혀끝은 아직도 얼얼해요.
examples.en: I drank hot tea, and the tip of my tongue is still numb.

explain: 혀의 맨 끝부분이에요. 맛이 남는다고 말할 때나 발음을 설명할 때 '혀끝에 남다', '혀끝을 대다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the very end of the tongue. It's often used in phrases like '혀끝에 남다' (linger on the tongue) when describing taste and '혀끝을 대다' (touch with the tongue tip) when explaining pronunciation.

examples.ko: 흰머리가 많아서 한 달에 한 번 염색을 해요.
examples.en: I have a lot of gray hair, so I dye it once a month.
I found a gray hair while looking in the mirror.
Grandmother's gray hair is pretty like silver.

examples.ko: 서른 살인데 벌써 흰머리가 나기 시작했어요.
examples.en: I'm only thirty, but gray hair has already started to appear.

examples.ko: 흰머리 때문에 나이가 들어 보인다고 해요.
examples.en: People say I look older because of my gray hair.

examples.ko: 흰머리를 뽑으면 더 난다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a saying that if you pull out gray hair, more comes in.

explain: 머리 전체가 하얀 것은 '백발'이라고 하는데 조금 격식 있는 말이에요. 젊은 나이에 난 흰머리는 '새치'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Hair that is white all over is called '백발', which sounds a bit more formal. Gray hair that appears at a young age is also called '새치'.
